why_this_matters: Day 130 sits in Phase 7 (Statistics), whose goal is: Describe data, quantify uncertainty and test hypotheses correctly. Today's core material - Paired t-test and repeated measures, One-way ANOVA logic, F-statistic and between/within variance - is the vocabulary the rest of the phase is built on. Learners who skip the concept and jump to copying code usually stall two weeks later; the goal here is that you can explain what you did, not just that it ran.

code.heading: Post-hoc Tests for One-Way ANOVA
code.code:
from statsmodels.stats.multicomp import pairwise_tukeyhsd
import numpy as np

# Sample data
data = {
    'Growth': np.concatenate([fertilizer1, fertilizer2, fertilizer3]),
    'Fertilizer': ['F1']*len(fertilizer1) + ['F2']*len(fertilizer2) + ['F3']*len(fertilizer3)
}

# Convert to DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Tukey's HSD test
tukey = pairwise_tukeyhsd(endog=df['Growth'], groups=df['Fertilizer'], alpha=0.05)
print(tukey)

code.heading: Post-hoc Tests for Two-Way ANOVA
code.code:
from statsmodels.stats.multicomp import pairwise_tukeyhsd
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.formula.api import ols

# Sample data
data = pd.DataFrame({
    "Growth": [20, 22, 19, 24, 25, 28, 30, 27, 26, 29, 18, 20, 22, 19, 24,
               21, 23, 20, 25, 26, 29, 31, 28, 27, 30, 19, 21, 23, 20, 25],
    "Fertilizer": ["F1", "F1", "F1", "F1", "F1", "F2", "F2", "F2", "F2", "F2",
                   "F3", "F3", "F3", "F3", "F3", "F1", "F1", "F1", "F1", "F1",
                   "F2", "F2", "F2", "F2", "F2", "F3", "F3", "F3", "F3", "F3"],
    "Sunlight": ["High", "High", "High", "High", "High", "High", "High", "High", "High", "High",
                 "High", "High", "High", "High", "High", "Low", "Low", "Low", "Low", "Low",
                 "Low", "Low", "Low", "Low", "Low", "Low", "Low", "Low", "Low", "Low"]
})

tukey = pairwise_tukeyhsd(data['Growth'], data['Fertilizer'] + data['Sunlight'], alpha=0.05)
print(tukey)

common_mistakes.mistake: Watching the lecture without running the repository notebook.
common_mistakes.why: Recognition is not recall: code that looked obvious fails the moment you type it yourself.
common_mistakes.fix: For every topic today, run the linked notebook cell, then retype it from memory in your own file.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using Paired t-test and repeated measures on data whose types or shape you have not printed.
common_mistakes.why: Most failures in this topic are input problems (dtype, shape, missing values) rather than logic errors.
common_mistakes.fix: Print type and shape immediately before the operation; keep that habit for all 275 days.

debugging.symptom: The linked notebook cell raises ModuleNotFoundError or ImportError.
debugging.cause: Wrong kernel/environment selected, or the library is not installed in the active environment.
debugging.fix: Print sys.executable in the notebook and install into that environment (Day 4).

debugging.symptom: Your output differs from the recording even though the code looks identical.
debugging.cause: Library version differences, a changed default argument, or unseeded randomness.
debugging.fix: Pin versions (requirements.txt), set a random seed, and compare dtypes and shapes, not just values (Day 5).
